result.topic_en: Euler combines the particular solutions for each admissible value of the angle ω into a general equation describing all possible vibrations of the elastic rod, then begins examining the fundamental tone (ω ≈ 3ρ) and its nodal points.

Scholion 1.
§. 20. Quodſi igitur pro ſingulis iſtis valoribus anguli $\omega$ formentur valores ipſius $y$, eorum quotcunque invicem coniuncti exhibebunt motus, quos noſtra virga recipere poterit. Si hoc modo omnes infiniti valores ipſius $\omega$ inuicem coniungantur, ac pro quolibet literis C et $\zeta$ generatim quicunque alii valores tribuantur, aequatio obtinebitur generalis, quae omnes plane motus, qui in virga locum habere poſſunt, in ſe complectatur. Haec igitur aequatio generalis, ſi valores anguli $\omega$ per $\omega$, $\omega'$, $\omega''$, etc. deſignemus, ſequentem habebit formam:
$y = C\,\mathrm{fin.}\,(\zeta + t\frac{\omega\omega c\sqrt{2gb}}{aa})$
$(e^{u\omega} \mp e^{\omega(1-u)} + (1 \pm e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{fin.}\,u\omega + (1 \mp e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{cof.}\,u\omega)$
$+ C'\,\mathrm{fin.}\,(\zeta' + t\frac{\omega'\omega' c\sqrt{2gb}}{aa})$
$(e^{u\omega'} \mp e^{\omega'(1-u)} + (1 \pm e^{\omega'})\,\mathrm{fin.}\,u\omega' + (1 \mp e^{\omega'})\,\mathrm{cof.}\,u\omega')$
$+ C''\,\mathrm{fin.}\,(\zeta'' + t\frac{\omega''\omega'' c\sqrt{2gb}}{aa})$
$(e^{u\omega''} \mp e^{\omega''(1-u)} + (1 \pm e^{\omega''})\,\mathrm{fin.}\,u\omega'' + (1 \mp e^{\omega''})\,\mathrm{cof.}\,u\omega'')$.
etc. etc. etc.
vbi litera $u$ denotat fractionem $\frac{s}{a}$, et ſigna ſuperiora valent ſi angulorum $\omega$, $\omega'$, $\omega''$ ſinus fuerint poſitiui, inferiora vero ſi fuerint negatiui.

Scholion 2.
§. 21. Quod ſi ſonum fundamentalem, quo eſt proxime $\omega = 3\rho$, et qui continet motum ſimpliciſſimum, quo virga contremiſcere poteſt, attentius conſideremus, facile colligere licet, curuam, quam virga inter vibrandum induit, axem ad minimum in duobis punctis ſecare debere,
Q 2 ita,

items.quote: aequatio obtinebitur generalis, quae omnes plane motus, qui in virga locum habere poſſunt, in ſe complectatur
items.english: a general equation will be obtained which contains in itself absolutely all the motions that can take place in the rod

items.quote: facile colligere licet, curuam, quam virga inter vibrandum induit, axem ad minimum in duobis punctis ſecare debere
items.english: it is easy to conclude that the curve which the rod assumes while vibrating must cut the axis in at least two points
